full_judgment:
3. Short facts of the case, are that the property in question was sold in auction for arrear rents in LR Sale Case No.1217 of 1952-53. One Abdul Latif Prodhan purchased the property in auction and got delivery of possession on 5-6-1955. Property under CS Khatian No.64 was in possession of one Bipin Behari Singh who refused to obtain settlement of the same on payment of rents to Abdul Latif Prodhan, consequently, the property was made khas by Abdul Latif Prodhan. In the way aforesaid Abdul Latif Prodhan while in possession and enjoyment of the property sold out a portion of the auction purchased property to the father of the plaintiff, Abul Khayrat Bhuiyan by a Registered Sale Deed No.4695 dated 22-6-1955. After death of Abul Khayrat Bhuiyan the plaintiffs as heirs acquired the property by inheritance and have been possessing the same in different ways by cultivating seasonal crops and rearing fishes in the low land. The defendants have had no title and possession in the property, but SA and RS khatians stood recorded in the name of vendors of the defendants who had no title and possession in the property. When the plaintiffs went to local Tahshil Office for payment of rents and mutation of their names, concerned officials refused to receive rent on the ground that khatian for the property stands in the name of defendant. Consequently, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.332 of 2015 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj for declaration of title and correction of the khatian against the government and others which is now pending for disposal. 

 7. The opposite-parties in their written objection against injunction application contended that the property originally belonged to Tarikanath Singh Roy and others. CS and SA khatian Nos.229 and 264 stood recorded in their names and RS Khatian also stood recorded in the names of some SA recordee and their heirs. The owners of the property while in possession and enjoyment by Deed No.7495 dated 8-9-1975 transferred the suit property to Amzad Hossain and 3(three) others and one Md Ramzan Ali purchaser of the property, by Deed No.1017 dated 6-2-2001 transferred the suit property to one Salema Begum and they got their names mutated in the khatian and paid rent to the government. They also claim that the plaintiff have no title and possession in the property for more than 60(sixty) years and did not pay any rent to the government and took no steps for correction of the khatian on the basis of purchase of their predecessor. The fact of dispossession by the defendants is false and fabricated. The plaintiffs never possessed the suit property but with the false allegation of dispossession filed the instant suit. 

 8. Mr Md Imam Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the property in question was put in auction in LR Sale Case No.1217 of 1952-53 which was purchased by one Abdul Latif Prodhan who got delivery of possession on 5-6-1955 and in support of such contention the plaintiffs could file some papers showing auction, Boinama and other connected papers. He further submits that the plaintiffs could file a Registered Deed No.4695 dated 22-6-1955 executed and registered by Abdul Latif Prodhan in favour of Abul Khayrat Bhuiyan, father of the plaintiffs and by the said deed vast property were transferred including the suit property. He further submits that except the suit plot other khatians for other property stood recorded in the name of the plaintiffs predecessor but inadvertently khatian for the suit property stood recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendants for which another title suit is now pending. He further submits that in the instant suit a complicated question of title is involved and that can be determination at the time of hearing on evidences. But the defendants being mighty persons took possession of the property by dispossessing the plaintiffs and trying to construct structure thereon by changing the nature and character of the suit property which will lead further complication and create multiplicity of judicial proceedings. He finally submits that pending determination of the merit of the suit, to prevent abuse of the processes of law and to secure ends of justice, both the courts below as well as this Court at the time of filing of the suit, appeal and this revision granted an order of status-quo directing both the parties which is continuing till today. Candidly, he submits that for ends of justice and to prevent multiplicity of judicial proceedings this Rule may be disposed of maintaining order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule directing the trial court to dispose of the suit within shortest possible time and in that situation parties to the proceedings will not be prejudice. 

 9. Mr Kazi Mujibur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos.1 and 3 submits that admittedly this is a suit for recovery of possession and declaration of title, meaning thereby, the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit property. He further submits that except some papers relating to auction and sale deed of the year 1955, the plaintiffs could not produce any paper showing recording of their predecessor's name or their names in the khatian, payment of rent and even not a single evidence of possession, as such, plaintiffs out of possession not entitled to get injunction. He further submits that in the event of decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiffs they will get possession of the property through court, as such, there is no earthly reason to prevent the defendants from developing the property by erecting structure or building thereon. He further submits that to get an order of injunction the plaintiffs must show a prima facie case, balance of convenience and inconveniences and irreparable loss, if the injunction is refused. But in the instant case the plaintiffs utterly failed to show a prima facie case in their favour and balance of convenience and inconveniences, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. From the statement made in the plaint as well as in the application for injunction, it appears that the property in question originally belonged to Tarikanath Singh Roy and 6(six) others as appearing from the khatian submitted by both the parties. The plaintiffs claim that the title of the CS recorded owner extinguish by auction sale in LR Sale Case No.1217 of 1952-53 and the property was purchased by one Abdul Latif Prodhan as appearing from Annexures-F series, annexed to the supplementary-affidavit filed by the petitioners. Said Abdul Latif Prodhan by a Sale Deed No.4695 dated 22-6-1955 transferred the suit property along with other properties to one Md Abul Khayrat Bhuiyan, father of the plaintiffs. Further it appears that SA and RS Khatians stand recorded in the name of the vendor of the defendants and the suit property in RS Khatian No.13 declared vested and non resident property. From Annexure-G1, annexed to the supplementary affidavit, it appears that the plaintiffs filed Tribunal Case No.63I2 of 2013 before the tribunal praying for release of the property from vested property list which was subsequently, abated and the property was released. 

 12. On the other hand, the defendants by filing relevant CS, SA and RS khatians tried to show that the property belonged to Tarakanath Singh Roy and 6(six) others subsequently, owner of the property and their heirs transferred the property to the defendants in the year 1975. The plaintiffs claim that the Deed No.7495 dated 8-9-1975 is a forged and fabricated document. In the Registration Office no such sale deed was found allegedly have been executed by Asish Ranjan Singh Roy and 5(five) others in favour of Amzad Hossain and 2(two) others.
